sources.title: Hefang Street Hangzhou Travel Guide 2026 | History, Culture & Top Attractions
sources.content:
Hefang Street Hangzhou: Complete Travel Information

Overview
Hefang Street is an 1,800-meter pedestrian street in Hangzhou's Shangcheng District. "One Hefang Street, Half of Hangzhou's History" captures its significance as a National Cultural Heritage Site dating to the Southern Song Dynasty when it was part of Lin'an, the imperial capital.

Address: 121 Gaoyin Street, Shangcheng District
Hours: 24/7 access; shops typically operate 10:00 AM–10:00 PM
Entry: Free
Suggested Time: 2-3 hours

Historical Significance
During the Southern Song Dynasty, the street served as a residential and commercial hub for royalty and aristocrats. It maintained prominence through Ming and Qing periods, preserving traditional architecture with characteristic green tiles and carved wooden details.

Main Attractions

Zhu Bingren Copper Sculpture Art Museum (Jiangnan Copper House): Features 1,215 copper artworks. Free admission, no reservation needed. Traditional Jiangnan architecture.

Hu Qing Yu Tang Museum: Historic traditional Chinese medicine store. Known as the southern counterpart to Beijing's Tong Ren Tang. Herbal tea tastings available. Admission: 10 RMB.

Former Residence of Hu Xueyan: Late Qing Dynasty mansion. Blend of traditional Chinese and Western architectural styles. Admission: 20 RMB. Hours: 8:00 AM–4:30 PM daily.

Southern Song Dynasty De Shou Palace: Royal palace site with Southern Song artifacts. Free admission with advance reservation via WeChat. Hours: 9:30 AM–5:00 PM (closed Mondays except holidays).

Exploration Route
Recommended sequence: Hefang Street → Southern Song Royal Street → Drum Tower → Hu Xueyan Residence → De Shou Palace → Da Ma Nong → Shi Wu Kui Alley

Dining Options

Panfang Chun Dumplings (Michelin Restaurant): Dumplings 1 RMB each, mixed noodles 7 RMB. Average cost: 16 RMB/person. Hours: 6:00 AM–2:00 PM. Address: 479 Zhongshan South Road.

Muslim Maji Palace Suniu Meat Pie: Crispy, fragrant meat pies. Average cost: 11 RMB/person. Hours: 9:30 AM–11:00 PM.

Dingsheng Gao Xiaodian – Jiang Shunfa: Traditional victory cakes symbolizing exam success. Average cost: 4 RMB/person. Hours: 9:00 AM–9:00 PM.

Shopping
Fang Huichun Hall: Traditional Chinese medicine products, mugwort compresses, pear syrup candies, fragrant sachets. Hours: 8:00 AM–9:00 PM.

Transportation
From Hangzhou City Center: Metro Line 7 to Wushan Square Station (Exit D), then walk to Hefang Street. Taxi: approximately 20 minutes, ~15 RMB.
From Xiaoshan Airport: Metro Line 7 to Wushan Square Station: ~1 hour 10 minutes, 7 RMB. Taxi: ~35 minutes, ~70 RMB.

Accessibility: The street has fairly level ground but can be narrow with heavy foot traffic. Strollers and wheelchairs may face challenges.

sources.title: Hefang Street: Step Back in Time in Hangzhou's Historic Heart | Wander in China
sources.content:
Hefang Street: Step Back in Time in Hangzhou's Historic Heart

Publication Date: September 1, 2025

Hefang Street serves as more than just a street; it's a living museum that transports visitors back to the city's rich past. The location features traditional architecture, bustling commerce, and aromatic offerings that provide insight into historical Hangzhou.

Historical Background
The street's origins trace to the Southern Song Dynasty (1127-1279) when Hangzhou functioned as China's capital. During this era, the area thrived as a commercial and cultural center, drawing merchants, artisans, and scholars. Contemporary shops represent descendants of these historical businesses, maintaining longstanding traditions and craftsmanship.

Why Visitors Come
The destination combines history, culture, and commerce in one location. People visit to experience old Hangzhou's atmosphere, taste regional food, acquire traditional crafts, and witness cultural performances.

What to Find There

Shops and Stalls: Establishments offer traditional Chinese medicine, silk products, handicrafts, and souvenirs. Visitors can discover silk scarves and locally-made items while negotiating prices.

Local Food: Notable snacks include Cong Bao Hui (scallion pancakes) and Ding Sheng Gao (steamed rice cakes). Tea houses serve Longjing tea for relaxation.

Traditional Arts: Artisans create sugar paintings, glass figurines, and calligraphy. Street performers present traditional music, opera, and puppet shows.

Visitor Guidelines
- Best Season: Spring or autumn with mild weather; Chinese New Year brings special energy
- Negotiation: Price haggling is standard practice
- Preparation: Expect significant crowds during peak periods
- Access: Public transportation provides convenient connection
- Conduct: Respectful dress and behavior honors local traditions

sources.title: Hefang Street, Hangzhou: History, Highlights, Location & Tips
sources.content:
Hefang Street, Hangzhou: History, Highlights, Location & Tips

Hefang Street, one part of Qinghefang Ancient Street in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China, features time-honored shops and museums providing a glimpse of Ancient Hangzhou culture and art.

Hefang Street is the most famous and the only well-preserved ancient street in Hangzhou. It boasts a history stretching back to the Southern Song Dynasty (1127-1279), when Hangzhou served as the capital of China.

Visiting Hefang Street is very relaxing where you can wander around at your own pace, and basically there are two things you don't want to miss: visiting traditional museums and browsing cultural and creative shops.

At the far end of Hefang Street are many stalls for street foods like crabs, squids, stinky tofu, BBQ, cool noodles and so on. There is a 140-year-old teahouse called Taiji Teaism where people like to have a cup of tea, listen to the popular tune and enjoy the performance of tea-brewing.

You'll find silk products, tea sets, calligraphy brushes, ink stones, ceramics, wood carvings, and local handicrafts. Bargaining is common and often expected at many of the souvenir shops.

To avoid the largest crowds, aim to visit on weekday mornings, as weekends and evenings tend to be much busier with both locals and tourists.

sources.title: Hefang Street - A Historic & Cultural Street in Hangzhou
sources.content:
Hefang Street - A Historic & Cultural Street in Hangzhou

Hefang Street is a famous pedestrian street in Hangzhou, stretching approximately 1,800 meters. Historically, during the Southern Song Dynasty, Hefang Street was part of the city of Lin'an (now Hangzhou) and served as a residential area for royalty, aristocrats, and influential figures, and was lined with bustling shops, restaurants, and teahouses, making it one of the most prosperous commercial areas of its time.

Getting There: The most common way is to take the Hangzhou Metro Line 1 or 4 to the Ding'an Road station, which is a short walk away. Driving directly to Hefang Street is not recommended as it's a pedestrian zone.

Hefang Street offers a vibrant glimpse into traditional Chinese commerce, crafts, and cuisine. Popular treats include Xiao Long Bao (soup dumplings) from Zhiwei Guan, Scissors Noodles from Zhang Xiaquan, fried Stinky Tofu, and Caramelized Chestnuts. It's within walking distance of the Hu Xueyan Former Residence and the China National Silk Museum.

Venture off the main drag into smaller lanes for a potentially more authentic feel and unique finds. Bargaining is expected at many shops. Comfortable shoes are a must!

sources.title: Hefang Street: Hangzhou Snacks, Museums & Nearby Attractions
sources.content:
Hefang Street: Hangzhou Snacks, Museums & Nearby Attractions

Hefang Street has free entry, though some attractions may charge an entry fee. The Hu Qing Yu Tang museum has 10 RMB admission, and the Copper Art Museum is free to enter with no reservation required and open from 9:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.

The street is open 24 hours, with most shops open from 10:00 to 22:00.

To reach it, take the metro to Ding'an Road Station (Line 1) or hop on bus routes 8, 13, or 71 to the Hefang Street stop.

Hefang Street, in the heart of Hangzhou, is a vibrant historic street famous for local snacks and unique cultural shops.

sources.title: 河坊街_百度百科
sources.content:
河坊街完整信息

基本信息
河坊街（Hefang Street），原名旬宣街、竹斋街，位于中国浙江省杭州市上城区境内的一条步行街、公路。河坊街中段为清河坊历史文化街巷景区的一部分，主路全部位于杭州西湖风景名胜区范围内。

规格参数：全长约1800米，起点江城路，终点南山路，宽度13至32米，道路等级城市次干路，商业建筑面积约18万平方米。

历史沿革

唐代（707年）：吴山东面钱塘江沙北涨，州司马李瑜开挖沙河（今中河），成为城边一条南北向的运河。

五代吴越国时期：在今鼓楼处置朝天门，河坊街逐渐成为一条日渐热闹的街市。

南宋绍兴间（1131—1162年）：杭州城向东拓展，河坊街上商铺林立，更加繁华，河坊街中段被称为清河坊，是连接宋高宗行宫宗阳宫和临安府治的要道。

1999年：杭州市确定河坊街为杭州历史文化保护区。
2000年3月：清河坊历史文化街巷保护工程启动。
2001年10月18日：河坊街中段以古文化街区开街。
2007年：被国家旅游局评为4A级国家旅游景区，成为中国首个被评为4A景区的商业特色街区。

票制票价：河坊街东西两段为城市次干路，无需票价。中段为杭州清河坊历史街区的一部分，景区免费。

客运流量：2024年5月2日15时，河坊街人流峰值达1.47万人，比2023年同期最高峰值增长18%。

历史建筑

方回春堂：创始于1649年（清顺治六年），有360多年历史的老字号国医馆。2001年10月重新开业。

胡庆余堂：胡雪岩在1874年创建的药铺，地处清河坊。是中国唯一一家双国宝单位。2006年，胡庆余堂中药文化入围首批国家级非物质文化遗产名录。

特色美食

西乐园羊汤：创始于清乾隆五十三年（1788年），有着200多年历史的中华老字号。

杭州定胜糕：南宋时百姓为岳家军出征鼓舞将士而特制的江南传统美食，为浙江省非遗美食。

文化特色
河坊街位于南宋都城临安城遗址的中心位置。其中'河'指的是当时的运河，'坊'则是指商业区或市集。闻名杭城的'五杭'也出于此(杭剪、杭扇、杭粉、杭烟、杭线)。

科博展馆
杭州世界钱币博物馆：成立于1999年，中国首批十大民营博物馆之一。
朱炳仁铜雕艺术博物馆：中国唯一的铜雕大宅，总建筑面积近3000平方米，共耗费原料铜125吨，被誉为'江南铜屋'。

价值意义
河坊街见证着杭州的千年变迁，也保留着老底子的文化记忆。（杭州市文化广电旅游局评）
河坊街，不仅是一条街道，更是一段承载着浓厚历史底蕴的文化长廊。（杭州市人民政府评）

sources.title: 2N1D in Hangzhou - West Lake & Hefang Street
sources.content:
2N1D in Hangzhou - West Lake & Hefang Street

Time seemed to pass slowly as you can leisurely walk around, have some finger food over some drinks and then shop again! Visiting Hefang Street is very relaxing where you can wander around at your own pace.

The street is an excellent place for souvenir shopping, with traditional Chinese crafts, tea sets, silk products, and various local specialties available. Bargaining is expected at many shops—start lower than you're willing to pay and meet in the middle.

While Hefang Street is always bustling, visiting during off-peak hours or exploring the smaller alleyways can offer a more genuine feel, and avoiding peak tourist times helps you better appreciate the architecture and local crafts.
